subject.title: Slack thread replies can be generated but not delivered after origin tuple is lost

question: Is the July 1 sanitized live evidence sufficient to start owner-directed design now, or should this stay blocked on a reduced QA flow that proves the exact Slack cleanup/recovery transition?
rationale: The source and discussion show a real delivery-reliability gap, but the current-main failing transition is not yet isolated enough for a safe autonomous repair without maintainer proof tolerance.

options.title: Wait for reduced QA proof
options.body: Keep the issue open with no new fix PR until a reduced Slack QA flow or sanitized event sequence ties origin tuple, persisted final, missing receipt, and cleanup/recovery completion together.

options.title: Start owner design now
options.body: Use the July live evidence to design the durable pending/failed delivery state at the send/recovery boundary, accepting that the first PR may need maintainer-owned iteration.

options.title: Fold into broad delivery contract
options.body: Track only the cross-channel durable-delivery contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 and close this Slack-specific item, losing some focused Slack incident evidence.

recommendation.title: Wait for reduced QA proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open with no new fix PR until a reduced Slack QA flow or sanitized event sequence ties origin tuple, persisted final, missing receipt, and cleanup/recovery completion together.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the current maintainer triage and has merged the adjacent fixes that define the remaining proof boundary.
